source: Philogelos (Hierokles und Philagrios, vermutlich 4./5. Jh. n. Chr.), Zaehlung nach Thierfelder 1968. Griechischer Text: tools/data/src/philogelos-greek.json (Eulogikon, Public Domain Mark). Die englischen Texte sind eigene Uebersetzungen.

fragments.reference_en: A scholar ordered a lamp from a silversmith. When asked how big it should be, he said: "Big enough for eight people."
A scholar nearly drowned while swimming. He swore not to go into the water until he had first learned to swim properly.
A man said to a scholar's doctor: "Doctor, when I get up from sleep I'm dazed for half an hour, and then I'm fine." The doctor said: "Then get up half an hour later."
Someone met a scholar and said: "Sir, I saw you in my dream." "I swear, I was busy and didn't notice you."
A scholar wanted to catch a mouse that kept eating his books. So he took a bite of meat and sat in the dark.
A scholar wanted to see whether he looked good asleep, so he shut his eyes and looked in the mirror.
A scholar bought a house, then leaned out of the window and asked the passers-by whether it suited him.
Someone told a scholar: "The slave you sold me has died." "By the gods," he said, "he never did anything like that when he was with me."
A scholar saw many sparrows in a tree. He spread out his coat and shook the tree, hoping to catch them.
A scholar who wanted to sleep had no pillow, so he told his slave to put a jar under his head. The slave said it was hard, so he ordered it filled with feathers.
A scholar was sailing in a fierce storm while his slaves wept. "Don't cry," he said, "I've freed you all in my will."
A dog bit a scholar's thumb. He said: "If it had caught my cloak, it would be torn."
One of two twin brothers died. A scholar met the living one and asked: "Are you the one who died, or your brother?"
A scholar wanted to cross a river, so he boarded the boat riding his horse. Asked why he didn't get off, he said: "I'm in a hurry."
A scholar who was selling his house carried a stone from it around as a sample.
A scholar saw a barge on the river, heavily loaded with grain. "If the river rises a little," he said, "it will sink."
Someone told a scholar with a skinny horse: "Your horse is looking toward Hades." The scholar said: "I can see that too."
A scholar who was ill and hungry was told that it wasn't yet the fourth hour. Not believing it, he ordered the clock to be brought to him.
A scholar carried out his son's body and met the boy's teacher. "Forgive me," he said, "that my son did not come to school. He has died."
A scholar learned that a ladder has twenty steps going up, and asked whether it has as many going down.
A scholar saw twin brothers and heard people marvelling at how alike they were. "This one isn't as much like that one," he said, "as that one is like this one."
A miser writing his will named himself as his heir.
An Abderite's sparrow died. Some time later he saw an ostrich and said: "If my sparrow had lived, it would be that big by now."
A chatty barber asked a witty man: "How shall I cut your hair?" "In silence," he said.
A doctor had given up on a sick man. When the man recovered, he walked a big circle around the doctor. Asked why, he said: "You told me I was dying, and I am ashamed to be alive."
A starving man saw a loaf of bread lying on a lintel. He said: "God, either lift me up, or bring that down."
A scholar met a doctor and said: "Forgive me, and don't blame me, that I haven't been ill."
A scholar learned that a raven lives for more than two hundred years, so he bought one to try it out.
A witty man was in court before a governor, who dozed off. He shouted: "I appeal!" "To whom?" "To you, awake."
Asked how many measures an amphora holds, a scholar answered: "Of wine or of water?"
